name: Forage Trails
desc: Ant-colony stigmergy in the open — several nests work an annulus of ground, foragers lay recruitment pheromone that other ants follow, sharpening aimless searching into hard trunk trails out to the food caches, until each cache drains, its trail evaporates away and the whole network rewires onto fresh ground; it never converges and never settles.

energy.doc: ant speed, pheromone deposit rate and trail-following sharpness

density.doc: colony size (280-1180 ants), number of nests (1-3) and number of food caches

speed.doc: rate multiplier on the whole colony

scale.doc: the foraging range the colony works, the sensor distance and cache size

evap.doc: pheromone evaporation — low leaves persistent trunk roads, high makes every trail ephemeral and the network rewires constantly

act.doc: cycle: food comes and goes on a slow arc · glut: rich caches everywhere, fat trunk trails · famine: thin pickings, the colony searches more than it carries

style.doc: field_plate: sepia ink on a toned buff field notebook page · pheromone: thermal false-colour, the chemical field alone · darkfield: the trails glow off a black ground · ink: pure tonal wash, no colour, no drawn ants
